modules.title: Singapore Sport In The 21St Century
modules.description: The process of change is just as apparent in sport as it is in any field of human endeavour. Sport in Singapore is a significant medium for social development that must also be seen to make contributions to the economy, to education, to social activity and to the creation of a national and an international identity. Government initiatives at the turn of the century are gradually being crystallised into meaningful actions affecting the wider population. Active participation in sport is encouraged and the status of sport as a potential career path is emerging more strongly.  Singapore has been recognised as a successful host of an increasing number of events, yet still requires affirmation of its competitive standards at international levels. This course will critically examine the nature and scope of sport related issues that have evolved during the 21st Century.

modules.title: Sport & Culture In Singapore: A Sociological Perspective
modules.description:
To "think sociologically" about sport which are closely connected with the Singapore context. 
	To examine the cultural foundations of sport, primarily from a Singapore perspective, but also considering international comparisons.
	To understand and critically evaluate social structures surrounding sport and culture by exploring concepts, theories, and studies (the body of knowledge) in the field of Sociology of Sport. 
	To review diverse social phenomena relating to sport that are experienced (seeing, hearing, feeling, and doing) in the real world using "sociological imagination".
	To articulate and present ideas and knowledge relating to sport in Singapore.

modules.title: Ethical Issues In Sport
modules.description: Sport is a socially significant activity for many individuals.  Moreover, the sports industry is global, saturates the media, influences young people and is a massive arm of the entertainment industry which generates billions of dollars each year.  The influence that such a massive industry plays on society generates a unique set of ethical issues.  This course will critically examine a number of the ethical issues surrounding the role of sport in society and ask the student to question and analyse the role of the sport in today?s world.

modules.title: Structural & Functional Anatomy
modules.description: This module deals with the various systems of the human body and the part each system plays in human movement. The aim of this module is also to enable participants to relate the structures and functions of the human body to physical performance, health and fitness. This module will also lay the foundation for further work in Exercise & Sports Physiology, Biomechanics and other disciplines in sport science. The mode of delivery of this module will be in the form of Lectures and Laboratories.

modules.title: Sociology Of Sport I
modules.description: The course focuses on cultural elements of the development of sport and physical activity in society today. The antecedents of today?s sport and physical activity patterns are examined in relation to changes in value systems that have occurred with the passage of time. Ranging from the origins of the Olympic Movement in Ancient Greece to the spread of a colonial model by the British, this course provides a foundation for sport studies of systems in many countries.

modules.title: Introduction To Sport Management
modules.description: The course provides students of basic introductions in the field of sport management. Definitions and disciplinary foundations of sport management will be presented. Basic concepts of sub-disciplines in sport management will be introduced.

modules.title: Introduction To Growth & Motor Development
modules.description: This course is designed for the understanding of physical growth and motor development, particularly during childhood and adolescence. The impact of age-related changes, individual and sex-differences, maturity-associated variation on physical growth and motor development will be covered.

modules.title: Health & Wellness I
modules.description:
Health & Wellness
	Heath Education, Prevention & Promotion
	Substance Abuse/Smoking
	Cancer/STDs & AIDS
	Nutritional Concerns
	Weight Management 
	Body Image Disorders
	Stress Management

modules.title: Exercise & Sport Physiology I
modules.description: A lecture/demonstration laboratory course is designed as a foundation course for the study of exercise physiology. Emphasis will be placed on; the energy systems that fuel muscular work, muscle fiber types, aerobic and anaerobic performance and training adaptations, blood lactate after exercise and maximal oxygen uptake. The importance of proper fluid management and aspects of thermoregulation during exercise in the local tropical environment will also be emphasised.

modules.title: Human Anatomy & Physiology
modules.description: The objectives of this course are to learn about the structures and functions of the various organ systems within the human body and the role of these systems in physical performance, health and fitness.

modules.title: Introduction To Sport Management
modules.description: The course introduces you to the field of sport management. Definitions and disciplinary foundations of sport management will be presented. Basic concepts of each sub-discipline will be introduced. Further, you will be given the opportunity to examine the current developments in sport management and related these trends to your career development. Essential topics in this course include definitions of sport management, careers in sport management, essential skills and roles of the sport manager, management functions, areas of study in sport management, and current trends in sport management.

modules.title: Introduction To Growth & Motor Development
modules.description: This course focuses on factors influencing physical growth and motor development, age-related changes, individual, gender-related and maturity-associated variations in growth and development. Individual differences during the pubertal growth period will be highlighted and discussed. Students will gain a better understanding of the impact of physical activities and sport participation during a Lifespan (especially in the early years) and its importance to the development of motor skills.

modules.title: Introduction To Health & Wellness
modules.description:
This course introduces Health & Wellness at the elementary level.
1.	Introduction to theoretical concepts of health & wellness, prevention, health education and promotion.
2.	Lecture series in nutrition, weight control, eating disorders, major diseases (cancer and heart diseases, STDs & Aids), stress management, substance

modules.title: Foundations Of Exercise Physiology
modules.description: This is a foundational course whose objectives are to provide information on how the human organ systems function during exercise and to examine how exercise training causes adaptations to those organ systems.

modules.title: Psychosocial Aspects Of Sport & Exercise
modules.description: This is an introductory course on exercise and sport psychology. The focus of this course is on the social and psychological aspects of sport and exercise. Topics covered include personality, motivation, stress and coping, aggression, moral development, team building and cohesion, competition, and leadership. Emphasis will be on the role of sport psychology in influencing participants? cognition, emotion, and behaviour in physical activity and sport settings.

modules.title: Outdoor Recreation
modules.description: This course introduces students to the outdoors as a recreational pursuit and explores its affordances for personal growth and team building, the development of confidence, problem solving skills, and leadership. Risks are inherent in the outdoors and an understanding and application of a risk assessment and management system will also be introduced. Through experiential learning at the Outward Bound School Singapore, students will be facilitated to experience and understand the outdoors and at the end, will be well-placed to organise, lead, and manage outdoor activities.

modules.title: Exercise & Sport Psychology 1
modules.description: This focus of this module is on the social and psychological aspects of sport and exercise. Topics covered include personality, motivation, stress and coping, aggression, moral development, team building and cohesion, competition, and leadership. Emphasis will be on the role of sport psychology in influencing participants' cognition, emotion, and behaviour in physical activity and sport settings.

modules.title: Motor Learning & Control 1
modules.description: This module is designed to provide students with background knowledge in motor skill acquisition. Emphasis is on the theoretical and practical nature of motor skill acquisition and retention in relation to motor-physical performances.

modules.title: Sport Biomechanics 1
modules.description: Biomechanics is the study of a biological system by means of mechanics. This module introduces the basic mechanical concepts and principles that govern human movement. The aim of this module is to enable participants to perform qualitative analyses of human movement using basic concepts of mechanics and anatomy. Basic quantitative analysis will also be introduced to allow participants to evaluate numerically the nature of the movement.

modules.title: Coaching & Learning 1
modules.description: This course examines and applies practical sport coach pedagogy (learning theories and instructional models) to the sport environment. The course also considers pedagogical knowledge and application of the principles of motor skills' learning.

modules.title: Physical Activity & Leisure For Special Populations
modules.description: THIS MODULE ADDRESSES PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES AND RELATED TOPICS TO IMPROVE FUNCTIONAL CAPACITY IN SPECIAL POPULATION INCLUDING VARIOUS CHRONIC DISEASE PATIENTS AND THE ELDERLY. PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL FEATURES OF CHRONIC DISEASES AND PRECAUTIONS AND GUIDELINES FOR EXERCISE WILL BE ADDRESSED.

modules.title: Research Methods & Design In Physical Activity & Sport
modules.description: This course provides students with a foundation from which to critically examine quantitative and qualitative research designs and strategies.  Every effort will be made to place such designs and strategies and their applications in basic or pure and applied settings of physical education and sport.  Specifically, the module introduces the student to: the nature of the research process, the use of literature, the definition and evaluation of a research problem, hypothesis formation, scientific investigation and methods, types of research available and abstract and report writing.

modules.title: Sport Injuries I
modules.description: This module is designed to provide students with fundamental knowledge and skills to prevent and manage sports injuries. The module covers background knowledge in dealing with sports injuries from first aid care to rehabilitation.

modules.title: Foundations Of Motor Behaviour
modules.description: This introductory course introduces key concepts of motor control and learning, with a strong emphasis on experiential learning via practical experience of skills learning. The course comprises of components such as the degrees of freedom problem, theoretical paradigms, process of learning, and instructional strategies related to motor skills learning.

modules.title: Introduction To Sport Biomechanics
modules.description:
This course introduces basic mechanical concepts, laboratory equipment and software to evaluate human movements: 
	Linear and angular kinematics
	Linear and angular kinetics
	Equilibrium
	Fluid mechanics

modules.title: Sport Coaching: Foundations Of Coaching
modules.description: This course examines and applies practical sport coach pedagogy (learning theories and instructional models) to the sport environment. Issues related to effective coaching of young athletes will be addressed. In addition, pedagogical knowledge and application of the principles of motor skills? learning will be covered in this course.

modules.title: Sport Marketing & Sponsorship
modules.description: This Sport Marketing and Sponsorship course is designed to provide fundamental theoretical and practical knowledge of marketing principle, techniques, and issues confronting professionals and sport science organizations today. A variety of marketing theories for sport and exercise programs are introduced through: quality knowledge dissemination (lectures), active class participation (discussions and presentations), and professional inquiry (business plan and proposal). Lecture will be delivered by using PowerPoint slides. Group discussions will be moderated by the instructor. You will work on group project papers and present those to the class.

modules.title: Seminars In Current Issues Of Sport
modules.description: The course will cover topical sport science themes relevant to athletic performance, including doping and drug use and the role of sleep in sport performance.  In relation to local athletes the effects of Ramadan on sport performance will be evaluated.  From the sport management perspective, emerging topics related to sport marketing in social media and video games and the role and effectiveness of sport sponsorship will be evaluated.  The organisation of major sporting events will also be discussed which is relevant to the recent major sport events (Formula 1, SEA Games) held in Singapore.

modules.title: Physical Activity & Leisure For Special Populations
modules.description: This is an experiential course designed to introduce students to the world of adapted physical activity, leisure and sport for individuals with special needs. Students will gain an overview of the various recreational and sporting activities available in Singapore, and be introduced to the different disability conditions and the sport played by different disability groups. Principles, guidelines and strategies for activity instruction will be gleaned through hands-on participation, class discussions and personal reflections.

modules.title: Research Methods & Design In Physical Activity & Sport
modules.description: This introductory research course covers the basic contents necessary for students to undertake undergraduate research. Topics covered include basic appreciation of the research process, various strategies for qualitative and quantitative research, and the communication of research.

modules.title: Fundamentals Of Sport Injuries
modules.description: This course introduces the students to fundamental understanding of causes and mechanisms of sport injuries, injuries to different tissues, common sport injuries and their prevention, management and rehabilitation.

modules.title: Management Of Sport Organisations
modules.description: This course covers the essential topics and concepts of organisational theories and behaviors to understand the management of sport organisations. Students will develop broad understanding of the nature of sport organisations, structure, design, planning, problem solving/decision making, and other various issues in managing sport organisations.

modules.title: Statistics, Measurement & Evaluation
modules.description: This course is designed to provide students with basic concepts of measurement and evaluation in sport science and management. In addition, the course will focus on fundamental concepts of statistics and the use of computers for data analysis. Accordingly, the module introduces students to measurement issues in the sport science and management contexts, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, the research process, the method of science, scientific investigation, the definition and evaluation of a research problem, hypothesis formation, and data collection.

modules.title: Applied Statistics
modules.description:
The objectives of this course are to 1) provide students with a well-rounded and solid foundation in statistics for sport and exercise science and 2) prepare them for more advanced or graduate statistical courses.
The course content will cover: 
Basic concepts in statistics
Application and interpretation of descriptive and inferential statistics for quantitative research including considerations for test selection, exploratory data analysis and assessment of inferential test assumptions

modules.title: Exercise & Sport Physiology Ii
modules.description: A lecture/demonstration laboratory course is designed for the study of selected topics   of exercise physiology. The principles of nutrition applied to sports performance and exercise will also be included. Emphasis will be placed on energy release and substrate utilization, energy metabolism during exercise, fluid intake and athletic performance, ergogenic aids, vitamins and minerals, the pre-game meal, sports anemia, nutritional considerations for the diabetic individual, lipid metabolism and coronary heart disease.

modules.title: Exercise & Sport Physiology Iii
modules.description: A lecture/laboratory course is designed to provide a basic framework that will aid the third year students in acquiring knowledge and technical laboratory skills pertinent to exercise physiology.  The laboratory techniques and knowledge will help students to understand the demands of training on the body and will enable them to prescribe exercise or training for optimal health and elite performance. Emphasis will be placed on the energy contribution during high intensity exercise, prediction of performance in endurance events, lactate threshold/ventilatory thresholds and maximal oxygen uptake. The importance of body composition and the different assessment modes will also be emphasised.

modules.title: Sports Injuries Ii
modules.description: Physical activity is associated with multiple health benefits and enhanced quality of life. Sports participation across populations in the society is on the rise. Moreover, there has been a significant increase in number of adventure sports participants in recent times. The injury risks, patterns, principles of management and preventive strategies are different in each cohort. This course is designed to provide students with knowledge and the understanding of population-specific sports injuries and skills for primary management of injuries and preventive strategies.

modules.title: Health & Wellness Ii
modules.description:
The course addresses current trends in health and wellness.
This could include a critical analysis of current problems and trends in basic health education that contribute to healthful living in community, home and school.

modules.title: Environmental Exercise Physiology
modules.description:
The objective of this course is to examine the responses and adaptations of the human body to exercise under different environmental conditions.  
The course content will: 
Describe how the body produces heat and how different environmental conditions affect heat loss.
Discuss the responses of the body to exercise in the heat and the need for fluid.
Examine how the body adapts to exercise in the cold and at altitude.
Examine the stresses to the body during diving.
Describe the changes to the body during microgravity.
Examine how air pollution affects exercising individuals.

modules.title: Exercise Prescription
modules.description: The objectives of this applied exercise physiology course are to know 1) the role of exercise and physical activity for health as an intervention to prevent and/or manage chronic health conditions and 2) the exercise prescriptions for select chronic health conditions.

modules.title: Applied Sport Injuries
modules.description: This course is designed to provide students with hands-on skills, exposure to technology, knowledge and the understanding of applied, population-specific and epidemiological aspects of sport injuries.

modules.title: Physical Activity & Health
modules.description:
The objective of this course is to examine how physical activity and inactivity influences a number of health and disease outcomes.  

The course content will: 
Describe the evidence linking physical inactivity with several common health conditions.
Understand how to assess common health conditions.
Examine how physical activity can be used in the prevention and treatment of a number of health conditions.

modules.title: Sport Nutrition
modules.description: The objective of this course is to learn about the role of nutrition in supporting the physical performance, health and fitness of athletes.

modules.title: Sport Biomechanics Ii
modules.description: This course introduces participants to quantitative methods for determining mechanical parameters of movement, namely linear and angular kinematics and kinetics. Through laboratory work, participants will also learn about the operation of the equipment associated with the measuring techniques in sports biomechanics. Participants will be introduced to the theory governing these measurement techniques and studies that use of these measurement techniques. The aim of the course is to enable participants to effectively analyse movement, explain causes of observed effects and to correct errors in physical performance in sports through the use of these quantitative methods.  Participants should have completed the mechanical and anatomical bases of human motion before enrolling for this course.

modules.title: Sport Biomechanics Iii
modules.description: This course will focus on the quantitative analysis of human movement.  Participants will learn how to design a quantitative analysis, collect, analyse and interpret data obtained from the equipment associated with the measurement technique.  From the analysis work of this course, participants will be expected to examine the relationship between performance measure and human motor system.  Participants will have the opportunity to explore the underlying processes that is involved in the production of this human movement.  The course will consist of theory and applied field work.

modules.title: Experimental Biomechanics
modules.description:
This course will introduce current experimental methods in the biomechanical analysis of human movement, including: 
Kinematic techniques
Kinetic techniques
Inverse dynamics

modules.title: Analytical Biomechanics
modules.description:
This course will introduce current analytical methods in the biomechanical analysis of human movement, including: 
Conceptual models
Physical models
Statistical models
Simulations models

modules.title: Exercise & Sport Psychology Ii
modules.description: This focus of this module is on psychology of sport and physical activity. The module is designed to provide students with an understanding of how psychological variables influence participation in sport and physical activity. The main focus is on the key motivational perspectives of exercise and sport but advance topics such as children in sport, burnout, psychology of injury and exercise psychology will also be covered.

modules.title: Exercise & Sport Psychology Iii
modules.description: The focus of this course is on theory, research and practices in sport and exercise psychology. This course includes an overview of varied psychology topics (e.g., individual differences/personality, social influence and group dynamics, diversity issues, and applied psychological skills). The main focus is to understand major theories and research as well as applying those theories and research findings to diverse sport and exercise settings. In addition, the development and evaluation of basic psychological skills training programmes will be introduced.

modules.title: Coaching & Learning Ii
modules.description: This course following on the work undertaken in Coaching & Learning  - Foundation 1 examines and applies practical sport coach pedagogy (learning theories and instructional models) to the sport environment.  The course also considers pedagogical knowledge and application of the principles of motor skills? learning.  This compulsory course critically examines and applies sport coach pedagogy (learning theories, preferences and instructional models as it relates to movement) to the sport environment.

modules.title: Coaching & Learning Iii
modules.description: The purpose of this subject is to explore the complexity of coaching at an elite level. Topics cover in this unit aim to help students acquire the knowledge and skill pertinent to the development of the elite athlete. Student will be required to attach themselves to an elite team and to a designated master coach in a sport of their choosing. Students will be encouraged to learn and work with the coach, with the aim of enhancing the quality of training sessions and improve athletes' performance.

modules.title: Advanced Topics In Exercise & Sport Psychology
modules.description: The focus of this course is on psychology of exercise and sport. The course is designed to provide students with an understanding of how psychological variables influence participation in physical activity. The focus is on the key motivational perspectives of exercise and sport. Advance topics such as children in sport, burnout, and psychology of injury will also be covered.

modules.title: Sport Psychology In Theory, Practice & Research
modules.description: The focus of this course is on theory, research and practices in sport and exercise psychology. The students will be introduced to the role of applied sport psychologist, the development and evaluation of basic mental skill training, and theories underpinning each mental skill. This course will be both theoretical and practical based on research evidence. In addition, the development and evaluation of basic psychological skills training programmes will be introduced.

modules.title: Sport Coaching: Theory To Practice
modules.description: This course builds on the work undertaken in the foundation of sport coaching and critically examines the understanding and application of sport pedagogy (learning theories and instructional models) to the sport environment. Students will be given opportunities to observe and sample some coaching sessions, mentored by experienced instructors/coaches. In addition, best practice from successful sporting countries will also be explored to give learners an international perspective in sport coaching.

modules.title: Motor Learning & Control Ii
modules.description: This course addresses behavioural aspects of human movement. Interpreting and intervening human performances from the psychomotor domain are the main foci of this course. Topics to be covered include practice conditions, feedback and skill acquisition, theories of motor learning, and measurements of motor performances.

modules.title: Motor Learning & Control Iii
modules.description: The purpose of this course is to examine the concepts associated with human movement from neuromuscular basis. The course covers important structures involved in motor control from anatomical, neurophysiological, and biomechanical perspectives, and addresses how they interact to control various body parts.

modules.title: Adapted Physical Activity & Recreation
modules.description: Individuals with special needs, like everyone else, need to develop efficient and proficient movement control in both fine and gross motor skills. Hence, physical activity professionals should equip individuals with special needs with the necessary skills and knowledge to participate in modified and regular games and sporting events.

modules.title: Motor Control & Learning: Theory To Practice
modules.description: This course focuses on the central questions of why, when, and how movements becomes coordinated over time by way of reflecting on current theories and research. In particular, the dynamical systems approach is adopted as the main theoretical paradigm. Topics related to complex systems, ecological psychology, degrees of freedom problem, perceptual-motor landscape, and specific practical strategies related to acquisition of skills will be covered.

modules.title: Adapted Physical Activity & Recreation
modules.description: This course will enable students to better understand disability sports and apply theoretical knowledge and understanding in coaching athletes with disabilities. Students will develop instructional coaching skills and learn how to plan, adapt and teach physical activities/sports & games that cater to the needs of individuals with special needs via the practical attachment.

modules.title: Sociology Of Sport Ii
modules.description: The theoretical contributions of Durkheim, Weber and the Marxists provide the backdrop for a study of the significance of sport within society during the twentieth and twenty first centuries. Themes and issues relating to the expansion of mass and elite sport are examined within local and international settings. Eastern and western perspectives of the significance of sport and physical activity are compared. Power relations and the accommodation of various groups within the sporting system are considered.

modules.title: Sociology Of Sport Iii
modules.description: The final course focuses on the growing significance of sport as a tool of nation building in Singapore. A social history of sport and physical activity in Singapore before and after independence provides a framework for understanding how sport and national identity have become interwoven. This course traces the involvement of government in the creation of a society that increasingly values sport as a complementary aspect of national growth and development.

modules.title: Sport Marketing & Sponsorship
modules.description: The course on sport marketing and sponsorship investigates the nature of sport products and the motivations of sport consumers.  The sport consumer types are identified and their behaviour discussed.  The essentials of marketing will be taught and related to sport.  Students of the course will be given opportunity to work on a sport marketing project to appreciate and reinforce the complexity and dynamics of sport marketing.  Sponsorship issues and strategies will also be covered including the relationship of sponsors to the sport, platforms and benefits of sport sponsorships.

modules.title: Event & Facilities Management
modules.description: Sport is often presented through events which can be major meets like the World Cup or Olympics or regional and local events like a school meet.  Students will through this course understand the importance of sport events and the decision making considerations of hosting an event.  Opportunities will also be provided for students to experientially learn event management.  Important to any sport event are the sport facilities which require strict compliance to specifications and maintenance.  The concept of a multi-functional sport facility will also be explored.  Risk management during events and in facilities management will be highlighted.

modules.title: Human Resource Management In Sport
modules.description: Managing human resources well is vital to any organisation.  Students of this course will first begin to understand the different functions of human resource management such as recruiting, inducting, developing, and assessing personnel of the organisation.  An important human resource asset to most sport organisation are volunteers.  The motivation to participate in sport and the strategies of retaining sport volunteers will also be discussed and explored.

modules.title: Legal Aspects In Sport
modules.description: Managing sport requires developing relationships between organisations, and between individuals representing the sport and organisation.  Students of sport management must have an understanding of the legal aspects of these relationships and the roles and responsibilities of sport officials.  Topics of this course include sources of law, duty of care of sport officials, the concept of tort and negligence, contracts, and others.  Sport tribunals and its conduct will also be covered.  Relevant case studies will be used for discussion and learning.

modules.title: Management Of Sport Organizations
modules.description: This course uses the essential topics and concepts of organisational theory to understand the underlying objectives and perspectives of managing sport organisations.  Students will develop from the course broad understanding of the nature of sport organisations, leadership, planning, problem solving and decision making and issues in managing sport organisations.

modules.title: Finance & Business In Sport
modules.description: This course develops in the student understanding of important financial concepts and systems.  Sources of sport funding are explored and how would sport organisation utilise such financial resources.  Fundamental principles of financial analysis, capital structuring and financial management are covered to develop better understanding of financial and business issues related to sport.

modules.title: Event & Facilities Management
modules.description: This course is designed to assist you in gaining a basic understanding of sport facilities/venues in relation to planning, designing, constructing, maintaining, and scheduling. You will be exposed to several financial strategies used in facility planning/development as well as risk management and safety concerns when operating sport venues and events. In addition, you will learn several factors involving in managing sporting events such as location, revenue, promotion, and developing successful sport sponsorship plans.

modules.title: Human Resource Management In Sport
modules.description: Managing human resources well is vital to any organisation. Students of this course will examine the different functions of human resource management such as recruiting, training and assessing personnel of the organisation. In particular, given the importance of volunteers in sport organisations, the course will also examine human resource practices specific to this segment.

modules.title: Legal Aspects In Sport
modules.description: The purpose of this course is to give the students in sport management department a conceptual foundation for understanding the law and its relationship to sport, recreation, and physical activities. The course explores the kinds of legal problems faced in the day-to-day operations of an athletic, sport program, physical education, and recreational activities into common sense perspective that is easily understood and remembered. It is not intended to teach all there is known about the law but instead to serve as an introduction to areas of law that most often have an impact on administrators, practitioners, and sport industry.

modules.title: Sport Media & Communication
modules.description: The course introduces you the sport industry?s multifaceted segment of sport communication through the media. The course includes communication theories, research articles in relevant disciplines and industrial insights and practice to explain the ways where individuals, media outlets, and sport managers to create and deliver messages to their target audiences. Further discussion focuses on the current issues in sport communication and media.

modules.title: Finance & Business In Sport
modules.description: The learning objective of this course is to introduce students to important financial concepts and systems. This will allow them to appreciate financial aspects of sport business and evaluate the financial position of companies through the analysis of financial statements.

modules.title: Leisure & Recreation Management
modules.description: The course explores the concept of leisure and recreation in historical and social perspectives. You will undertake independent study of your leisure and recreation environment and suggest strategies to effectively meet the needs and demands of such activities. More importantly, this module is designed for final year students who are interested in advanced leisure and recreation management studies. This course provides you with exposure to reading, interpreting, critiquing, and presenting data from relevant studies. Specifically, you will take opportunities to explore the evolution and development of management theories through a series of extensive reviews of literature with particular emphasis on the different context of leisure/recreation management such as service quality, intramural sport, outdoor education, tourism, older adults? leisure, SNS and leisure.

modules.title: Sport Retail Management
modules.description: The learning objective is for students to learn about retail management theories and apply them to the sporting goods industry. In addition, students are expected to extend their understanding of sport marketing theories into the retail industry.

modules.title: Advanced Topics In Sport Marketing & Sponsorship
modules.description: The learning objective is for students to extend their knowledge in sport marketing and sponsorship. In addition, students are expected to apply their knowledge and conduct simple research studies in the area of sport marketing and sponsorship.

modules.title: Sport In Society
modules.description:
To critically examine the significance of sport from social, political, economic and cultural perspectives. 
To critically examine the significance of sport to different groups of people in Singapore 
To study different theoretical approaches to the sociology of sport. 
To describe and analyse the historical trends affecting sport in general and physical activity in Singapore specifically 
To develop analytical powers through interaction and discussion 
To increase personal factual knowledge of sport through reading and access to alternative forms of sport information

modules.title: Sport Technology, Innovation & Entrepreneurship
modules.description: This course introduces fundamental topics related to sport technology, innovation and entrepreneurship. Contents related to sport engineering, making and coding culture, sport materials and wearable technologies, and data analytics are covered to provide students with broad-based knowledge regarding sport technology and innovation. Students will also be guided to program and prototype a sport or movement related electronics gadgets. The last component of this course concerns the development of business plans.

modules.title: Health & Wellness Iii
modules.description: The emphasis in the course is on the nexus between nutrition, fitness and exercise. The effects of nutrition and exercise as prophylactic interventions for common diseases will also be covered. This includes a review of current research in nutrition, fitness and exercise and efficacy of nutritional interventions for exercise performance, fitness and wellness.

modules.title: Leadership & Instruction In Physical Activity & Sport
modules.description: This course is characterised by a myriad of complex processes involving strategic and analytic thinking, vision and detailed planning, and ongoing authentic creation of a physically literate learning community. At the heart of successful leadership is a passion for learning underpinned by a set of essential skills and qualities that enable the leader to perform their key leadership tasks in physical activity and sport.  Those who succeed in physical activity and sport tend to be leaders who draw on their personal values and abilities to maintain and develop a culture of learning and achievement, whilst simultaneously managing the ongoing tensions and dilemmas that emerge in any physical activity or sport program.  Leaders can exhibit a range of leadership styles, which become successful when they reflect the needs of their setting combined with their own deep motivations.  It is essential that leaders of physical activity and sport understand the need to reflect on their own performance and engage in their own process of continuous learning and development.

modules.title: Leisure & Recreation Management
modules.description: The course explores the concept of leisure and recreation in historical and social perspectives.  What are some of the current needs and issues of leisure and recreation?  How are leisure and recreation planning and programming done?  What are the areas in leisure and recreation?  Who are important stakeholders in any leisure and recreation planning and delivery?  Students will undertake independent study of their leisure and recreation environment and suggest strategies to effectively meet the needs and demands of such activities.

modules.title: Quality Management In Sport
modules.description: The concept of total quality management in sport is presented and students will have the opportunity to discuss and explore the important factors that contribute towards a quality sport organisation.  Case studies are used to reinforce the essential factors of quality management.  Strategic planning, leadership and efficient and effective work processes are highlighted as important enablers towards quality.  Some quality management frameworks are explored to understand the issues and concepts of achieving excellence.

modules.title: Track And Field
modules.description: This course aims to provide NTU students with the basic sports science knowledge and skills of running, jumping and throwing so as to execute and appreciate Track & Field events.  Based on a systematic and hands-on approach to this course, the students will have an enjoyable time learning how to execute events such as long jump, hurdles, sprints, high jump, javelin and discus throw. This course includes the principles of training and five core bio-motor abilities so as to equip the students with the fundamental skills and knowledge to design his/her own training program.

modules.description: This course is structured to provide a concept (understanding different dance elements and terminology) and practice-based understanding of dance, specifically jazz and dance sport. Basic movement activities including locomotor movements, use of space, use of dynamics and original dance patterns. Social dances include Samba, Waltz and Cha-cha.

modules.title: Aquatics
prerequisite: No injuries/med cond100m recogn stroke nonstop/tread1.8 1min
modules.description:
The course aims to develop stroke competencies and techniques in swimming. Participants will be expected to practice, acquire and finally, demonstrate correct and efficient technique in a least three out of the four swimming strokes (frontcrawl, breaststroke, backstroke and butterfly).

Related activities will also be introduced in the course:
	Basic Personal Survival and Life Saving Techniques
	Fundamentals of Water Polo
	Canoe Polo Basics
	Organising Swimming / Water Sports Events

modules.title: Introductory Swimming
prerequisite: No skills in basic swimming.Cannot read if passed SS9401
modules.description:
The course aims to provide NTU undergraduate students with the basic skills and knowledge required to learn how to swim.  Participants will learn the correct techniques required to swim the four strokes (frontcrawl, backstroke, butterfly and breaststroke). Skills like threading water, plunges/starts and turns/somersaults will be taught. In addition, FINA rules relating to these strokes will be introduced.

Students who read SS9401 Aquatics cannot read SS9402 Introductory Swimming.
